## M-099 Path jail — pure layer DONE (2026-11-06 keeper tick)
- Base: team-05 freshly reset to banked base f9df631 = M-098 closure (98/272). Built ONLY the pure layer in team-05; no push, no README touched, no config_defaults / config_catalog / PUBLIC_API / OWNERSHIP / CAMPAIGN_STATE / roadmap files touched.
- Existing confinement found (composition, not duplication): mythic_agent/core/workspace.py already ships the elder single-root road — resolve_file / assert_within_workspace / canonical_workspace_root resolve symlinks with Path.resolve and raise SecurityError on escape, and the live file tools ride it today (agents/tools.py resolves reads/writes through resolve_file; core/validation.py checks file-tool args against the workspace the same way). That road knows exactly one root, answers by raising, and carries write-specific refusals of its own (workspace root itself + .git on writes) — it has no named grants, no allow/deny decision as data, no stored gate, no /pathjail grammar. core/permission_profiles.py (M-095) binds paths only as a coarse read/write posture word; core/policy.py ToolPolicy authorizes by tool name/mode with no path binding at all; core/sandbox.py guards commands and core/os_sandbox.py (M-097) plans command confinement — neither judges file-tool paths. M-099 was therefore built as the missing judge composing with the elder road, not replacing it: the jail is the confinement decision, the elder resolve_file road keeps its own write rules.
- Built: mythic_agent/core/path_jail.py — validated grants (one grant = one absolute directory path, realpath-normalized; a relative grant refuses; duplicates dropped; one malformed grant refuses the whole list; grants are directory prefixes — file-vs-directory on disk is data, the prefix is what is judged) + check_path/decide_path, one mechanical judge: relative candidates resolve against the workspace, then os.path.realpath resolves the whole candidate BEFORE judging; allow iff the resolved path is the workspace root itself or inside it, or a grant root itself or inside it, with inside judged on path components via os.path.commonpath (the /ws2-vs-/ws sibling-prefix trick never matches); default deny fail-closed; malformed candidates (empty, non-text, NUL-bearing) are DENIED as decisions while malformed workspace/grant data raises (stored-data rule) + JailDecision as data (to_record type path_jail_decision) + JailRefusal shaped as news exactly like the network gates (type path_jail_refusal, news true, surface session_event, plain headline) — included because a file tool reaching outside the jail is an escape attempt with the same news value as a refused network reach + PathJail dataclass holding only the grants (the workspace root is the session's project root, supplied per check as jail.check(path, workspace_root)) + gate readers (enabled_from_config ships on / non-bool raises, grants_from_config absent = no grants, jail_from_config, set_enabled + GateChange with event type path_jail_setting_changed) + shared /pathjail parser (show/on/off/grants/check <path>/grant <abs-path>, grant validated in the parser) and formatters (format_path_jail renders PLAIN_EXPLANATION + setting line + resolved workspace + grants + a sample allowed check, format_grants, format_jail_decision, format_refusal, format_gate_change: "The path jail is now on/off."). The module judges only: no file opened, written or read, no setting mutated.
- Symlink-resolution honesty note: symlinks are RESOLVED (os.path.realpath) before judging, never assumed away — a symlinked directory inside the workspace pointing outside is denied for paths through it, and a symlinked directory outside pointing in is judged by its resolved path. For a candidate that does not exist yet, realpath resolves the deepest existing ancestor and the remaining tail is judged lexically beneath it; that is stated in the module docstring, and it is safe for the honest reason that a tail that does not exist cannot itself be a symlink — the moment any part of it exists as a link, resolution follows it (pinned by the nonexistent-tail-through-a-symlink-escape test).
- Verification on the laptop: tests/test_path_jail.py 35 passed (pure, TIER: integration, REAL directories + REAL symlinks in tmp_path); neighbours tests/test_network_gates.py + tests/test_permission_profiles.py + tests/test_os_sandbox.py 155 passed combined.
- Owed coordinator deltas at banking: catalogue S-91 for the new path_jail setting + S-92 for path_grants (next free ids after S-89 network_gates / S-90 network_allowlist), config_defaults lines path_jail: true + path_grants: [], PUBLIC_API + OWNERSHIP regen, roadmap flip M-099 to done (99/272 at banking), ledger row; dead-code quarantine entries if the banking gate flags the new Agent-facing surface (M-074 pattern).
- Still owed before M-099 can bank: agent layer (Agent path-jail status/set/grant methods, journal-first with save-failure revert; the live file-tool roads judged through the jail — check_path asked before a file tool touches a path, denials surfaced through the path_jail_refusal record as session news; grants stored as plain path strings under path_grants) + /pathjail wiring on terminal and TUI roads + chat_screen help/usage/routing; then coordinator banking in roadmap order (merge → full suite → regen → closure → explicit-refspec push → ls-remote verify).

## M-104 The Keeper pattern built in — pure layer DONE (2026-11-06 keeper tick)
- Base: team-10 verified at banked base 16764f2 = M-103 closure (103/272). Built ONLY the pure layer in team-10; no push, no README touched, no config_defaults / config_catalog / PUBLIC_API / OWNERSHIP / CAMPAIGN_STATE / WAVE_PLAN / roadmap files touched.
- Existing basis found (composition, not duplication): the keeper law is Volmarr's own standing design, worked by hand over this campaign — a ten-minute minder that checks whether guarded work has stopped and continues it itself, never merely reporting. M-103 ships the watched work itself as data (managed background jobs with live tails and completion news) but nothing in the tree judges whether a piece of work has gone quiet too long or says what is owed when it has. M-104 was built as that missing judgement ON the M-103 sibling pattern, not replacing it: the same frozen validated dataclasses, build_/validate_ pairs with alternate spellings, PLAIN_EXPLANATION, USAGE, shared parser and formatters, deterministic-id registry, and *_record functions shaped as session news returning None when not applicable.
- Command-surface name chosen: /keeper — the slice's own title word, in the one-word lowercase house style of /background, /hookpacks, /plan; no /keeper surface existed in the tree.
- Built: mythic_agent/core/keeper.py — KEEPER_SLICE = "M-104" + WATCH_KINDS (background_job / crew_member / task; kind words read case-insensitively with dashes as underscores, unknown kinds refuse) naming WHAT is watched (a background job from M-103, a crew member's task, any tracked task) + WatchTarget frozen dataclass validating on construction (optional target_id — an empty one refuses; non-empty label; stall_after_seconds a whole number 60..86400, default 600 — the 10-minute keeper cadence — with booleans refused; last_activity_at an epoch float >= 0, default 0.0; restarts a count >= 0, default 0; max_restarts 0..100, default 3, booleans refused) + validate_watch_target / build_watch_target for mapping data (kind or type, label or name, stall_after_seconds or stall_after, last_activity_at or last_seen_at, restarts, max_restarts, target_id or id; conflicting spellings refuse, unknown keys refuse, one bad value refuses) + record_activity (a copy with the activity clock advanced; an earlier moment raises — time never runs backwards) + WATCH_STATUSES (active / quiet / stalled) with judge_watch returning a WatchVerdict frozen dataclass (target_id, kind, label, status, age_seconds, action): age is now minus last activity (a negative age raises), younger than half the bound is active, at or past half but under the bound is quiet, at or past the bound is stalled + ACTIONS (none / restart / report): active and quiet owe none, a stalled target is owed restart while restarts remain and report when they are exhausted — the keeper law as a mechanical reading, restart the work and surface it when restarts run out, never silently watch forever + intervention_record(verdict, target) returning the session-news dict (type keeper_intervention, news true, target_id, kind, label, status, action, age_seconds, restarts, one plain headline line) when an action is owed, else None (the block_record / completion_record pattern) + record_restart (a copy with restarts + 1 and its clock reset to the restart moment; refuses when restarts already equal max_restarts — an exhausted target is reported, not restarted past its bound — and refuses a backwards moment) + KeeperRegistry (register / get / list_targets in registration order with an optional kind filter / heartbeat recording activity on the stored target / check returning every target's verdict in registration order / interventions returning only the non-None intervention records; caller-supplied ids used as given with duplicates refused, unsupplied ids are the deterministic sequence watch-1, watch-2, ... skipping numbers a supplied id already took, mirroring BackgroundJobRegistry; unknown ids raise KeyError) + PLAIN_EXPLANATION (the keeper notices work that has gone quiet, restarts it while restarts remain, and reports it when they run out — a timer that works, not a timer that watches) + USAGE and the shared parse_keeper_args for the future /keeper surface (show, show <target>, check, heartbeat <target>; a grammar word in the wrong shape is a USAGE error, never a target id, mirroring parse_background_args) + formatters (format_watch_target, format_watch_targets with the plain "Keeper watches: none." empty statement, format_verdict, format_intervention, format_keeper the whole slice) with the stall state stated in words wherever shown and a stalled target's line stating its age and its owed action (restart or report) — status never carried by colour or symbol alone. The module holds watches and verdicts as data only: it runs no process, starts no timer, writes no file, changes no setting, and imports no agent / UI code.

- Built in team-10 only, on the M-103 sibling pattern exactly: Agent holds a KeeperRegistry for the session (lazy `_keeper_registry()`, session state, no new setting — the registry is session work exactly like M-103's job registry). ## M-108 agent layer DONE (2026-11-07 keeper tick)
- Built in team-04 on the M-108 pure layer (3f4e434 + 5c26369, on banked base 1221753 = M-107 closure, 107/272), following the M-107/M-106 sibling pattern exactly: Agent holds a HaltRegistry for the session, created lazily on first use (no new setting — a halt is session work, exactly as M-103/M-104/M-105/M-106/M-107 hold theirs). Methods: _kill_switch_registry (the held registry lives under the attribute _kill_switch_halts_registry — a first cut stored it under the method's own name and the getter returned the bound method; caught by the agent tests and fixed to the sibling pattern, e.g. _fleet_registry / _fleet_mode_registry) / kill_switch_status (held halts as plain records + every judged verdict held alongside its halt + format_halts_screen + PLAIN_EXPLANATION; a status read registers, judges, halts and publishes nothing) / get_halt / get_halt_verdict (the historical verdict judged at the pull, never re-judged from later holdings; None when unjudged; unknown ids raise KeyError on every road) / _kill_switch_holdings + pull_kill_switch + _publish_kill_switch_pulled (below).
- The real-usage road (_kill_switch_holdings) reads every holding from a road that really holds it — nothing invented: the coder is active exactly when its turn lock is held (a turn in flight holds it); background jobs are the held M-103 jobs with their real lifecycle states; crew tasks are the held M-106 tasks — a task with a finished verdict is finished, a task backed by a live background job (the road fleet_check runs a task through, the job carrying the task's display label) is running, any other task is merely queued, a plan and not held work (fleet ids are fleet-N, learned from the runner, not task-N as first assumed in the tests); pending approvals are read from the approval road itself — approvals are asked one at a time under the tools layer's approval lock (agents/tools.py prompt_approval_sync), so a pending approval exists exactly while that lock is held and there is never more than one.
- pull_kill_switch (a Halt, a halt mapping, or field words; nothing named halts all four targets) registers the halt, reads the holdings, and lets the pure layer judge the pull against that moment's holdings; it then carries the halt out through the REAL roads — held live background jobs are killed through the M-103 road (kill_background_job: request recorded, real process terminated, kill applied, completion published), a running crew task is halted on its backing job through that same road (a crew-only pull kills only crew-backed jobs; a crew with no live backing job has nothing running to kill and the verdict says nothing held / already stopped rather than claiming a halt that never happened — there is no separate crew kill road in the tree, and none was faked), and the coder + pending approvals are halted by setting the coder's own cancellation event (Agent.cancel): in-flight work stops at the next runtime boundary and a pending approval, which waits on that same event, is refused — it raises its cancellation and is never answered as approved; there is no separate approval road, and the docstring says plainly that refusing an approval rides the coder's cancellation event because that is the road approvals are bound to. The kill_switch_pulled record is published as session news through _checkpoint, announced at most once per pull (keyed by the halt's fresh id). The return names the jobs actually killed and any kill that refused, in words. NO mid-turn interception beyond the cancellation event's own boundary stops is claimed, and no mid-edit state is invented.
- Surfaces: /halt on terminal + TUI roads sharing parse_halt_args + the pure formatters (show -> the kill-switch screen; show <halt> -> format_halt with its held verdict, an unknown id answered in words; pull / pull <target> -> pull_kill_switch with actor "user" and the post-pull screen) + the terminal help line + chat_screen help/usage/routing.

NO new setting — a trail is session work, exactly as M-103's job registry, M-104's watch registry, M-105's schedule registry, M-106's fleet registry, M-107's budget registry and M-108's halt registry are held. Methods: audit_status (held entries as plain records + the registry's whole-trail export + format_audit_screen + PLAIN_EXPLANATION; a status read appends and publishes nothing) / get_audit_entry (KeyError passthrough) / audit_export (the export as plain data + format_export text, both from the same registry; exporting publishes nothing) / record_audit_entry (the explicit road: pure build_entry readings, append, publish; refuses loudly on a bad spec or a held id, exactly as the pure registry refuses) / _publish_audit_record (the pure layer's audit_recorded record journaled through _checkpoint when a session is attached, announced at most once per entry, keyed by its fresh id).
- Feeding from the REAL roads, as acts happen — every feeder rides _record_audit_note, which appends and publishes but never raises: recording must never break the road it rides on, and a dropped note never changes the act, which already happened or was already refused (the explicit record_audit_entry road is the loud one; only the as-it-happens notes are silent). The roads: (1) TOOL CALLS, EDITS and TOOL-ROAD COMMANDS from _execute_call, the funnel every tool call in a session travels — trailed exactly once per call from a finally block, so granted, refused, failed, interrupted and cancelled calls each leave exactly one entry; the kind is the tool's own (run_command = command, write_file / replace_file_content = edit, every other tool = tool_call), the actor is the coder, or the crew when this agent is a named subagent rather than the Primary (a spawned agent's acts are crew acts, and its own trail says so), the target names what the act touched (the command line, the file, or the tool), and the detail is the OUTCOME WORD alone (completed / permission denied / failed / refused / interrupted / cancelled) — a tool result's text is never trailed, because a result may be a whole file's contents. Programmatic apply_* edit calls under the funnel are the machinery an edit travels, not separate session acts, and are not trailed separately (no double count: one write_file call leaves exactly one entry, pinned by test). (2) APPROVALS from the two approval callbacks the tree actually builds — Agent.bind_tui's approve closure (the TUI road) and terminal.configured_agent's approve closure (the terminal road) — at the moment the human's answer lands, actor human: a remembered approval answering (M-096 road, checked first in both closures) or the prompt answered granted or refused; a prompt cancelled before any answer is not an approval and is never trailed as one. There is no third approval road in the tree, and none was faked. (3) BACKGROUND COMMANDS from start_background_job, called where the job visibly lives beside _keeper_note_background_activity — started jobs, and a command the OS could not start at all (its honest 127 ending, held as a failed job, trailed as the attempt it was); the actor is the crew when the job carries a held fleet task's display label (the reading M-108's holdings use to tell running crew work) and the coder otherwise, so fleet commands are crew work and the trail says which it was rather than guessing; fleet checks and keeper restarts ride this same road and are trailed there, never twice. (4) HOOKS from run_hooks, as each hook's run is judged — a hook run is a command with actor hook, its target the hook's command line and its detail the verdict's decision and exit code; hooks fire only through run_hooks in this tree, there is no other hook firing road, and none was invented.
- Surfaces: /audit on both roads sharing parse_audit_args + the pure formatters (show -> audit_status screen; show <entry> or a bare entry id -> format_entry, an unknown id answered in words with the registry's own "unknown audit entry"; export -> format_export via audit_export; a grammar word in the wrong shape is the USAGE, never an entry id): terminal.py handler + the terminal /help line; command_handler.py _handle_audit + /audit routing mirroring _handle_halt (bold-cyan publication, usage/KeyError published in red); chat_screen.py help line, usage entry, and system-command routing list all gained /audit.

- Command-surface name chosen: /doctrine — the slice's own subject word, in the one-word lowercase house style of /audit, /halt, /secrets, /budgets; checked first: no /doctrine surface and no doctrine command existed in the tree (the only doctrine mentions are prose in method_charter.py), and no destructive_doctrine module name clashed.
- Built: mythic_agent/core/destructive_doctrine.py — DESTRUCTIVE_DOCTRINE_SLICE = "M-111" + DOCTRINE_RUNGS (reversible / costly / irreversible — exactly the roadmap's three words in roadmap order; NO extra safe base rung was added, because no sibling doctrine carries one and an unplaced command is handled honestly as unclassified instead) + APPROVAL_REQUIREMENTS (none / ask_once / explicit_named_targets — none for reversible, ask_once for costly grounded in the permission-profile ask answer and the ToolPolicy ask mode, explicit_named_targets for irreversible grounded in M-096's explicit rule) + APPROVAL_PHRASES saying each approval in plain words + DoctrineRung frozen dataclass (also exported as Rung: the approval is derived from the rung when unnamed and a rung built naming any other approval refuses, so a rung never promises less than the doctrine asks) + DOCTRINE_LADDER held as validated data + rung_for / approval_for_rung / validate_rung / build_rung + DestructivePattern frozen dataclass (pattern_id via normalize_pattern_id, rung via normalize_rung, label as clean text, regex validated by compiling it, an anchor word targets are read after, and an implicit_target phrase held as data for acts whose command names no target) + validate_pattern / build_pattern / pattern_for_id + COMMAND_PATTERNS, the 29 held shapes as validated data in the judge's precedence order (the dry_run reading first — a command declaring --dry-run, or git clean / push -n, changes nothing; then the irreversible shapes; then the costly shapes; then the reversible readings — so an act matching two rungs earns the worse one) + judge_command, the mechanical judge (a command text, or its argv words as data; patterns read in held order and the first match places the act; a command no pattern matches is judged unclassified — no rung, no pattern, approval ask_once — and is never claimed safe; an empty command refuses) + DestructiveJudgement frozen dataclass (also exported as Judgement: command + argv as data; a classified judgement must name a held pattern of its own rung and carries that rung's one approval; an unclassified judgement names no rung and no pattern; the classification, pattern and approval are validated against each other on construction so a judgement can never disagree with itself; a judgement on the irreversible rung REFUSES to exist without at least one named target) + plain_words, the roadmap's rule as code (for an irreversible act the sentence names every target and says it cannot be undone before anything else; costly names its targets and its price; unclassified states plainly it is not claimed safe) + doctrine_record returning the session-news dict (type destructive_act, news true, judgement id, command, argv, rung, classification, pattern, approval, targets, and the plain-words headline) for EVERY judged act — a judged destructive act is always news, never lost as a log line (the M-108 halt_record pattern) + DoctrineRegistry, an in-memory storage-neutral registry model (register / judge judging and holding in one move / get / list_judgements in the order judged / record announcing one held judgement; caller-supplied ids used as given with duplicates refused and unknown ids raising KeyError, unsupplied ids the deterministic sequence judgement-1, judgement-2, ... skipping numbers a supplied id already took — no randomness a test cannot pin) + PLAIN_EXPLANATION + USAGE and the shared parse_doctrine_args for the /doctrine surface (empty/show -> ("show", None); ladder -> ("ladder", None); show <judgement> or a bare judgement id -> ("show", judgement); check <command...> -> ("check", command) with everything after check taken as the command however many words it takes; a grammar word in the wrong shape — a bare rung word, a bare pattern id, check with no command — is a USAGE error, never a judgement id) and formatters (format_rung / format_ladder stating every rung's approval in words, format_pattern / format_patterns naming every held shape with its rung, format_judgement with rung and approval always stated and an unclassified judgement stated as not classified and not claimed safe, format_judgements with the plain "no commands judged" empty statement, format_doctrine_record / format_record, format_doctrine_screen the whole slice — status stated in words wherever shown, never colour or symbol alone). The classifier's shapes, stated plainly: irreversible — rm with recursive+force in any flag spelling (short combined, split, or long), mkfs / mke2fs / mkswap, shred / wipefs / blkdiscard, dd of=/dev/..., redirection onto a raw block device, DROP TABLE / DATABASE / SCHEMA and TRUNCATE TABLE in a command, git push with --force / --force-with-lease / -f, git reset --hard, git clean with -f, and the fork bomb; costly — any other rm, redirection overwriting a file (a /dev/null target excluded), git push, git reset, git checkout -- / git restore discards, git branch -d / -D, mv, recursive chmod / chown, kill / killall / pkill, piping into a shell, shutdown / reboot / poweroff, truncate, and find -delete; reversible — the dry-run reading, read-only programs (ls / cat / grep / echo and kin with no destructive shape), git status / log / diff / show and kin, branch switching, and mkdir / touch. Targets are read mechanically per shape: a redirection names its file, a dd names its of= device, a drop names its database object, other shapes name the operands after their anchor word, and an irreversible act naming no operand takes its pattern's held implicit_target phrase (a bare force push names "the current branch on its remote", a bare hard reset names "uncommitted work in the working tree", a forced clean names "untracked files in the working tree", a fork bomb names "every process on this machine") — named from held data, never guessed at judge time. The module holds the ladder, the patterns and the judgements as data only: it runs no command, deletes nothing, writes no file, changes no setting, and imports no agent / UI code (stdlib re / shlex only).

A custom office id must not name ANY shipped office - not one of the six formalised offices, not the shipped polymath / guardian crew offices, and never primary (the lead session itself) - and the refusal names the boundary it hit. A custom office therefore cannot silently collide with, shadow, or override a formalised office, and a formalised OfficeDefinition offered to the custom machinery refuses plainly (it is already held by M-122). - Design, in the M-132 review-panels shape exactly: the shared project memory is the union view over per-member notebooks. A MemoryEntry is one fact in exactly one member's notebook (member as an M-121 member id composed by import from core/crew_members.normalize_member_id, never re-implemented; a short title; the fact in plain words; tags naming its topics, each once, possibly none; and its provenance). A MemberNotebook holds one member's entries in file order and judges: no foreign member's entry, no duplicate entry id inside it, no duplicate fact inside it (fact text compared case-insensitively with whitespace folded; the same fact in two DIFFERENT notebooks is two members' records and stands, pinned by test). A CrewMemory judges the whole: one notebook per member, entry ids unique across the whole memory, and its shared entries() view is derived in one deterministic order (member id, then entry id). FINDABLE BY ALL is search_memory / find_entries: exact + substring matching over entry ids, member ids, titles, fact text and tags, every query word required to match, run over the union of all notebooks; an asking_member argument is validated and then deliberately does NOT narrow the search, so the auditor's fact is found when queried as the scribe - pinned by test. There are no embeddings, no model calls and no relevance scores. Search is DERIVED from the held entries at call time, never stored: no record holds a search result or an index. The registry (CrewMemoryRegistry) holds notebooks entry by entry with deterministic entry-N ids for id-less entries, refusing a duplicate entry id anywhere and (through the notebook judge) a duplicate fact in one notebook and a second notebook for one member. Records (entry_record / notebook_record / memory_record) are shaped as session news off the pieces' to_record; /memory grammar is shared via parse_memory_args (show / show <member> / bare member / search <words> / tag <tag> / entry <entry-id> / members) with format_entry / format_entries / format_notebook / format_notebooks / format_memory_screen over PLAIN_EXPLANATION + USAGE. Records entry_record / report_record / ledger_record / book_record shaped as session news (type cost_court_entry / cost_court_report / cost_court_ledger / cost_court_book, slice M-140, news + headline). Plain words (plain_words per record, report_plain_words and ledger_plain_words per record or book), formatters (format_entry / format_entries / format_report / format_ledger / format_cost_court_screen) and the shared parser parse_cost_court_args for the /costcourt grammar.

- Design, mirroring the M-139 failure-fostering agent layer exactly, adapted to a registry holding one record kind: a session CourtRegistry on Agent, lazily held behind _cost_court_registry(), the attribute named _cost_court_store (never the method's own name), session state only - NO config delta, NO new setting. Read roads cost_court_status / get_cost_entry / cost_report / scribe_ledger (plus the book road cost_court()) register, hold and publish nothing (pinned against a real SessionStore); they answer from the held registry first when the session holds any run record, and from the shipped example only while nothing is held - a held session answers for its own book alone: a record, member or slice the held book does not hold raises KeyError with no fall back, on every read road alike. The report and ledger roads derive at call time from held records - cost_report naming the member and the slice, scribe_ledger naming no argument - so a total is never held stale; the registry holds run records and never reports or ledgers, so a book registered whole answers with reports and the ledger derived at call time, while a book recorded whole stands whole as the session's - its held ledger and all - through _cost_court_held (pinned by test both ways). Records held one by one stand under a session cost court book (title "Session cost court book") composed from the held records in the agent layer, so a later whole book recorded under its own title is never refused by a shim title at the registry (a whole book recorded after one-by-one holdings still refuses, on the registry's own duplicate entry-id refusal, pinned by test). Holding roads register_cost_entry / register_cost_book / record_cost_book publish each held record's entry_record as session news through _checkpoint via _publish_cost_court_record, deduped per entry id, foreign record types refused on that road (cost_court_report / cost_court_ledger / cost_court_book / failure_report / crew_replay_step / character_voice_profile / crew_sizing_case / stand_up_entry / crew_memory_entry / panel_review / crew_member / external_seat all pinned as refused). register_cost_book registers a whole book's records through the registry in book order, while record_cost_book(book=None) records a whole book once - the shipped example by default, or a book loaded via the pure load_cost_court_file road - the same book twice refusing (fingerprinted on its entry ids + title), publishing the entry records in book order and remembering the book whole as the session's. Report road report_cost_court renders the held book (or the shipped example when unheld) through the pure formatters alone (format_entries / format_report / format_ledger / format_cost_court_screen) and registers and publishes nothing. The /costcourt surface rides BOTH roads (terminal + command_handler + chat_screen routing/help) sharing the pure parse_cost_court_args + pure formatters (format_entry / format_entries / format_ledger): show / entry <entry-id> / member <member-id> / slice <slice-id> / ledger; the surfaces' member word renders through format_entries' member filter and the slice word through the held book's entries_on read over format_entry, since the pure entries formatter filters by member alone. Honest boundary pinned by test: no generate / persist / bill / charge / live-crew / board road exists on the agent - this layer calls no model, bills no one, charges nothing, runs no live crew, persists nothing and claims no crew run happened live.

A per-part report is DERIVED from that part's records in held order - its entry ids, builds, distinct slices, distinct members and account read off the records - never stored loose: a stored report whose fields or account disagree with the derived report refuses, and a report naming no account refuses too. The coordinator's ledger is DERIVED from the whole book: its rows are the per-part reports in the order the records first name each part, its totals are the rows' sums (builds summed, slices counted distinct across rows, parts counted as rows - a ledger whose totals are not its own rows' sums refuses at construction) and its account is read off the rows; a stored ledger whose keeper, rows, totals or account disagree with the derived ledger refuses, and the keeper is always the coordinator (COORDINATOR_KEEPER) - the discipline the roadmap words name, and NOT a casting member: the shipped offices note names the lead session itself the coordinator, never a working office, so the keeper word is this slice's own constant (asserted by test against load_casting()). Alias spellings throughout (entry_id/id, member/member_id, slice/slice_id, title/name; entry_ids/entries, builds/build_count, slices/slice_ids, members/member_ids, account/statements; keeper/coordinator, rows/reports, the total_* names with their shorter spellings) with the two-spellings-with-different-values refusal and the unknown-key refusal on records, reports, ledgers, the guide head and the top-level mapping. Registry: DogfoodRegistry holds build records in held order with deterministic dogfood-N auto ids, duplicate entry id refused, first book sets the title, reports and the ledger derived at call time and never held. Records entry_record / report_record / ledger_record / book_record shaped as session news (type dogfood_entry / dogfood_report / dogfood_ledger / dogfood_book, slice M-141, news + headline). A ConnectedNode is one piece of connected code grown from one seed: its path and symbol, its kind (the graph's definition kind, or the honest word - file, module, unresolved), its relation in the closed RELATIONS set in ranking order (seed, definition, caller, callee, reference, import, imported-by, file-neighbour), its distance (0 only for the seed piece itself), its seed's score kept whole - the piece's rank is DERIVED at call time, the seed score halved at each hop (GRAPH_DECAY 0.5), a stored score judged against the derivation and refusing on disagreement - its seed's id, and its provenance in plain words. THE EXPANSION (expand_retrieval) walks the graph from each seed: the seed itself, the definitions beside it in its file, its anchors' callers, callees and reference sites, the files its file imports, the files that import it, and its file's other graph neighbours at distance 1, and at depth 2 (MAX_RETRIEVAL_DEPTH) the symbols met at distance 1 grow their own callers, callees and references one hop further. HONESTY, pinned by tests: a seed naming a file the graph does not hold, or a symbol its file does not define, grows nothing and stands in the bundle's skipped with its reason - never silently relocated (a misplaced symbol names where the graph does define it, in the reason); pieces beyond the node cap are counted in omitted, never silently dropped; ranking is deterministic (score, distance, relation, path, symbol, line - two expansions of the same seeds stand in the same order, pinned); retrieve() marries both roads (symbol mentions + semantic scores, merged per site keeping the better score) and refuses when neither road names a seed - returning the whole repo would be confetti, not retrieval. The BUNDLE holds query, seeds, pieces in ranked order with positional node-N ids, depth, omitted and skipped, its totals and relation counts derived and any stored ones judged, and its account derived (a stored account disagreeing refuses). The PANEL is DERIVED from a bundle by derive_panel (rows the pieces carried whole in ranked order; totals the pieces' own counts), judged by validate_panel against its bundle and refusing on any disagreement. The shipped yaml holds ONE example book in exactly the shape a real book file takes - the M-151 slice boundary, one retrieval whose semantic seed names the compaction glass-box record, grown one hop into six pieces (the panel defined beside it, the agent road that calls it, the token estimator it calls, a test that references it, the budget file its file imports), with its one stored panel (panel-m151-boundary, rows node-1..node-6 in ranked order) equal to the derived one and pinned by the loader (require_example); plus a loader for a book file anywhere on disk. Records shaped as session news (node_record / bundle_record / panel_record / book_record, types graph_retrieval_node / graph_retrieval_bundle / graph_retrieval_panel / graph_retrieval_book, slice M-152, news + headline), plain words (plain_words per piece, panel_plain_words per panel or book), formatters (format_node / format_nodes / format_seeds / format_panel / format_graph_retrieval_screen), the shared parser parse_graphsearch_args for the /graphsearch grammar (show / node <node-id> / seeds / panel), and GraphRetrievalRegistry holding bundles one by one with deterministic retrieval-N auto ids and duplicate-id refusal. - What the repo already ships, found and composed (never duplicated): (1) Where things stand already ships as data - the stand-ups (core/stand_ups.py, M-134) hold the coordinator's digest (done / doing / blocked / needs-you) derived from its entries, session memory (core/session_memory.py, M-153) holds a session's situation across days, multi-session per project (core/multi_session_projects.py, M-162) holds parallel sessions each under its own journal, and long-session endurance (core/long_session_endurance.py, M-161) holds a long session's measured budgets; a handoff standing beside one of those holdings is that holding read onto this layer BY IMPORT (handoff_from_stand_up / handoff_from_session_situation / handoff_from_parallel_session / handoff_from_endurance_record, each judged by its own layer's validate_* road, plus handoffs_from_multi_session_book over whole multi-session books and registries, and inspect_handoff_source judging a piece by the layer that owns its type). Only the piece's references and counts cross the seam: from a stand-up only the digest's entry ids cross (never an entry's title, detail or member); from a situation only its session reference and the ids it itself names (its carried notes, open slices and standing decisions) as evidence; from a parallel session only its project, branch, session reference and its own journal's entries as evidence; from an endurance record only the reference it stands under and its provenance. - Design, in the M-162 multi-session shape exactly, with the handoff summary standing where M-162 held the parallel session: a HandoffSummary is one ended session's standing written durable, carried with its provenance whole - its title, the session it ends (session_ref), its project, the branch it stood on, the four claim sections in the stand-up's own CLAIM_KINDS set (done / doing / blocked / needs_you, judged by the stand-up layer's own normalize_status road), the session and journal evidence those claims stand on (evidence_refs), who wrote it (written_by), the ISO written_on day, and where it was read from (source). CLAIMS CARRIED, NEVER INVENTED IS THE LAW, pinned by tests on both layers: a handoff's claims are the stand-up digest sections of its session carried by entry id alone - a claim stands in one section only, a handoff naming no claim at all refuses, and a claim is handed off once in a book (a second handoff naming a held claim refuses, naming both sessions). EVIDENCE WHOLE IS THE LAW, pinned further: a handoff naming no evidence refuses, because a handoff standing on no evidence states nothing that can be checked, and validate_handoff judged against a stand-up report, registry or digest refuses a handoff whose four sections disagree with the digest that evidence derives - a handoff states only what its evidence states. ONE HANDOFF PER SESSION IS THE LAW: a session ends once, and a second handoff naming a held session refuses, in a book and in the registry alike. THE HANDOFF PANEL is DERIVED from the whole book by derive_panel: its rows are the book's handoffs carried whole, in settled order (by project, then day, then branch, then title, then handoff id), its totals are the handoffs' own counts (handoffs, their claims in all, their evidence references in all) and its section counts the claims' own per-kind tallies; validate_panel judged against a book refuses a stored panel whose rows, totals, counts or account disagree with the derived one, and handoff_refs / total_claims / total_evidence read the visible surface off any book or registry. THE HANDOFF VERDICT is DERIVED for the whole book by derive_verdict: awaiting-you when any claim needs the human's word, held-up when claims stand blocked and none needs you, standing-clear when neither stands - a stored verdict whose word is not its own tallies' word refuses at construction, because what needs you is never smoothed away. The shipped yaml holds ONE example book in exactly the shape a real book file takes - the M-162 slice boundary: 3 handoffs of the one mythic-agent-coder project, each standing on the journal entries of its own session from the multi-session book (the endurance session closed on main with 4 claims - 2 done, 1 doing, 1 needing Volmarr's word - on 2 evidence references, the graph-retrieval session paused on work/graph-retrieval-care with 1 done and 1 blocked on 1, the token-thrift follow-up closed on work/token-thrift-followup with 1 done on 3; 7 claims in all, no claim shared, 6 evidence references) - with its one stored panel (panel-m162-boundary, 3 rows in panel order) equal to the derived one and pinned word-for-word by the loader's example check, and its derived verdict awaiting-you. HandoffRegistry holds handoffs one by one under deterministic handoff-N ids, never panels or verdicts (both are derivations, read at call time); a whole book is judged whole before its handoffs are held in book order. A handoff standing in this layer is a recorded writing only, never a claim that anything was sent to the next session or human. ## M-163 addendum - Agent method shadowing fix (2026-11-09 keeper finisher, team-09)

- Defect (keeper-diagnosed from the merged-tree full suite, repo/logs/m163-fullsuite.log; reproduced in team-09 before the fix): M-163's Agent methods get_handoff (llm.py, ex-line 28264) and register_handoff (ex-line 28294) redefined the M-126 crew-comms Agent methods of the same names (llm.py:12821 / 12892). Python keeps the last definition, so crew-comms callers holding a crew Handoff hit the handoff-summary versions and raised ValueError (a handoff summary is needed). Pre-fix evidence in team-09, slice+crew combined: 7 failed, 85 passed - all 7 in tests/test_crew_comms.py (TestCrewCommsAgentRegister x6 + TestCrewCommsAgentStatus::test_status_after_register_shows_the_held_handoff).
- Fix: renamed ONLY the M-163 Agent methods - get_handoff -> get_handoff_summary, register_handoff -> register_handoff_summary (llm.py, 2 def lines). Only the pieces' ids, sections and standings cross the seam: from a map only its entry ids and the sections they stand in; from a ledger only its candidate ids and each candidate's standing - never an entry's or candidate's title, detail or provenance words (pinned by blob tests on both composition roads). (2) The import/export search was made and recorded: no portable-memory layer ships in the tree - /memorymap holds the map and /ledger holds the ledger, neither packs the two together as a file that rides with the repo - so this slice is that packing layer, and it invents no sending, posting, file-writing or live-memory-applying road of its own (the patch exchange's export/import and the audit export are different contracts on different slices, searched and left alone). - Design, in the M-163 handoff shape exactly, with the memory package standing where M-163 held the handoff summary: a MemoryPackage is one project's map + ledger exported as one portable file record, carried with its provenance whole - its title, the project it packs, the session it was exported from (source_session), the map entry ids riding and the closed map sections they stand in (in MAP_SECTIONS order), the ledger candidate ids riding and the promotion states they stand in (in PROMOTION_STATES order), who exported it (exported_by), the ISO exported_on day, and where it was read from (source). IDS ONLY ACROSS THE SEAM IS THE LAW, pinned by tests on both layers: a package names what rides by id, section and standing alone. JUDGED WHOLE BEFORE ANYTHING IS HELD IS THE LAW, pinned further: validate_package judged against a named map or ledger source refuses a package whose ids, sections or states disagree with the holdings it packs, unknown keys refuse by name (a foreign record never rides), and the registry's register_book judges a whole book - and the held book beside it - before holding any of it, so a clashing book holds nothing at all (pinned: the first package of a clashing book never lands). A PIECE RIDES ONCE IS THE LAW: an id stands in one side of one package only, and in a book one session's export of one project stands once and no piece rides in two packages, in a book and in the registry alike. THE MEMORY PANEL is DERIVED from the whole book by derive_panel: its rows are the book's packages carried whole, in settled order (by project, then day, then title, then package id), its totals are the packages' own counts (packages, map entries, ledger candidates, pieces) and its ride counts the pieces' own per-kind tallies (map / ledger, the RIDE_KINDS set); validate_panel judged against a book refuses a stored panel whose rows, totals, counts or account disagree with the derived one, and package_refs / total_map_entries / total_candidates / total_pieces read the visible surface off any book or registry. THE PORTABILITY VERDICT is DERIVED for the whole book by derive_verdict: fully-portable when every package rides map and ledger both, map-only or ledger-only when no package rides both and only one holding rides at all, partially-portable otherwise - a stored verdict whose word is not its own tallies' word refuses at construction, because a partial packing is never smoothed into a whole one. The shipped yaml holds ONE example book in exactly the shape a real book file takes - the M-163 slice boundary: 2 packages (the mythic-agent-coder project packed whole from the handoff-day session - its 9 map entries of all four sections and its 3 ledger candidates standing candidate, promoted and declined; the samtal project's map packed alone from its gatekeeper session, 2 entries, architecture and gotcha - 14 pieces in all, no piece shared), with its one stored panel (panel-m163-boundary, 2 rows in panel order) equal to the derived one and pinned word-for-word by the loader's example check, and its derived verdict partially-portable (1 riding both, 1 map-only). The shipped example's first package is exactly the pure composition of the shipped M-150 map book and M-155 ledger book, pinned by test. MemoryPackageRegistry holds packages one by one under deterministic package-N ids, never panels or verdicts (both are derivations, read at call time); a whole book is judged whole before its packages are held in book order. A package standing in this layer is a recorded packing only, never a claim that anything was sent, written into a repo, or applied to any live memory. - Agent layer, mirroring the M-163 agent layer exactly: a session MemoryPackageRegistry on Agent, lazily held behind _memory_import_export_registry(), the attribute named _memory_import_export_store (never the method's own name, the M-108 lesson), session state only - NO config delta (search recorded in the design bullet above). Reads (memory_import_export_status / get_memory_package / memory_import_export_panel / memory_import_export_verdict / report_memory_import_export) register, hold and publish nothing; they answer from the held registry first when the session holds any package, else the book recorded whole, else the shipped example - a held package answers for its own book alone, an id the held book lacks raises KeyError with no silent fall back to the example. Packages held one by one before any whole book stands recorded stand under a book composed in the agent layer, so a later whole book recorded under its own title is never refused by a shim title. Holding roads (register_memory_package / register_memory_package_book / record_memory_package_book) publish journal-first package/panel news through _publish_memory_package_record via the checkpoint road, deduped per shape, foreign record types refused on that road; record_memory_package_book(book=None) records a whole book once - the shipped example by default, or a book loaded via the pure load_memory_import_export_file road - the same book twice refusing (fingerprinted on its package ids + title), publishing the package records in book order then the derived panel record, and remembering the book whole as the session's with its held panel answering. THE EXPORT ROAD (export_memory_package) is this slice's own composing road: the session's memory map book (M-150) and ledger book (M-155) are read onto a package BY IMPORT and held - the books' entry/candidate ids, sections and standings alone (pinned: no entry or candidate title, detail or provenance word stands in any record or headline the road publishes), the derived panel and verdict of the whole held registry are published as their news records, and the road mutates no live holding: the session's map and ledger books stand exactly as they stood (pinned). THE IMPORT ROAD (import_memory_package) holds a package judged whole first: the pure validate_package road judges provenance, contents and counts together (unknown keys refusing by name) before the registry holds anything, so a malformed or foreign package refuses with nothing held and nothing published (pinned). HONEST BOUNDARY, pinned by tests on both layers: data only - holding, recording, exporting or importing a package sends nothing, posts nothing, schedules nothing, ends no live session, calls no model, writes no workspace file, persists nothing beyond the session journal news, and WRITES NO LIVE MEMORY: importing leaves the session's own memory map book and ledger book byte-identical in ids and decisions, holding and exporting leave every workspace file byte-identical and a ContextBuilder's built messages byte-identical (all pinned); the pure module imports no agents, ui or terminal code (its imports are the shipped core layers alone) and the Agent grows no send, post, schedule, apply, persist or board road under a package name. - What the repo already ships, found and composed (never duplicated): the memory stores themselves already ship as data on shipped roads - the project memory map (core/project_memory_map.py, M-150), session memory across days (core/session_memory.py, M-153), cross-project memory (core/cross_project_memory.py, M-154), the self-improving ledger (core/self_improving_ledger.py, M-155), crew memory (core/crew_memory.py, M-133), the subconscious v2 (core/subconscious_v2.py, M-165), the contradiction watch (core/contradiction_watch.py, M-166) and private by architecture (core/private_by_architecture.py, M-167). What none of those layers held is the health of the stores themselves: which stored pieces fail their own layer's validation, which vector records name memories no store holds, and which map entries point at paths that moved - so this slice's findings are composed BY IMPORT from those holdings (finding_from_map_entry, finding_from_session_note, finding_from_cross_project_lesson, finding_from_ledger_candidate, finding_from_crew_entry, finding_from_subconscious_memory, finding_from_contradiction_watch, finding_from_privacy_posting), each piece judged by its own layer's validator, ids and refs only across the seams. Doctor search recorded: mythic_agent/doctor.py already ships the `mythic doctor` health-check registry (config / workspace / tools / sessions / dependencies / provider), and the command handler's /doctor is the shell-command fixer with its own grammar - so the memory checks ride (a) a new `memory` health check in doctor.py that loads all nine shipped memory store books through their own loaders and fails plainly naming a corrupt store (it reports corruption; it repairs nothing), and (b) a new /memorydoctor session surface beside the other memory books, because the session's held books live on the Agent, not in the CLI process. Config search recorded: no doctor / registry setting ships for any sibling slice and none was needed - NO config delta.
- Design, in the M-167 private-by-architecture shape exactly, with the memory finding standing where M-167 held the privacy posting: a MemoryFinding is one check stood over one stored memory, validated as data WITH ITS PROVENANCE WHOLE - the check that raised it (corrupt-store, orphaned-vector or map-drift - the roadmap's own three), the stored memory it stands over, named by the kind of holding it stands in (memory-map, session-note, cross-project-lesson, ledger-candidate, crew-fact, subconscious-memory, contradiction-watch, vector-record or manual - the M-167 kinds carried whole) and the shipped piece's id alone, the store the memory lives in (the workspace store or the user store), what the check saw in plain words, how far the trouble reaches (contained to one piece, or store-wide), who ran the check, the session it ran in and where the finding was read from. The repair is DERIVED, never chosen: disposition_of and repair_action_of read it off the finding's check and extent alone - quarantine-piece for a contained corrupt piece, drop-orphan-vector for an orphaned vector, realign-map-entry for a drifted map entry - and a store-wide finding derives REFERRED_ACTION (none-referred) and stands referred to the user, so the doctor never quietly attempts what it should not. The three checks run genuinely, by import: finding_from_corrupt_piece judges a raw store piece by its own holding's validator and raises a finding only where the validator refuses (a sound piece raises "no corruption found"), finding_from_orphaned_vector stands a vector record's ref against the refs the held stores carry, and finding_from_drifted_map_entry stands a map entry's named path against the paths actually present. One finding per check per stored memory stands in a book, so a check's word never forks (the same memory under a different check is a different finding, and stands). The doctor panel is derived from the whole book (every finding carried whole, in a settled order - by check in the roadmap's order, then title, then finding id - its derived repair shown on every row), a doctor verdict is derived for the whole book (sound for none referred, ailing for one or two referred, critical for three or more), and the repairs are derived from the whole book as DoctorRepair records, each judged against its finding. Shipped example book at the M-167 boundary (mythic_agent/data/memory_doctor.yaml): 5 findings - a contained corrupt ledger candidate, an orphaned vector, two drifted entries, and one store-wide corrupt subconscious store referred to the user - four safely repairable and one referred, its derived verdict ailing, the stored panel pinned equal to the derived. 76 public names in core/memory_doctor.py. HONEST BOUNDARY, pinned by tests on both layers: applying a derived repair marks the held finding repaired in the registry's / session's own book only - it rewrites no live store, deletes no memory and writes nothing to disk, and no road here repairs a live store, wipes a store, or carries a finding anywhere. Data only beyond that: this layer sends nothing, posts nothing, schedules nothing, calls no model and persists nothing beyond the session journal news.
- Agent layer, mirroring the M-167 agent layer exactly: a session DoctorRegistry on Agent, lazily held; a register road holding a finding judged whole before it is held (its finding record published once, deduped per shape); a corrupt-store road (check_memory_store_piece) judging one raw store piece by its own layer's validator - its id alone crossing, the piece itself never held - publishing finding, panel and verdict news; a check-run road (run_memory_doctor) running the orphaned-vector and map-drift checks over the session's own held memory books by import (privacy-book vector postings stood against every ref the held books carry; path-like map refs stood against the project root's actual paths; findings already standing are skipped, never duplicated; the held books stand exactly as they stood - held books are validated by construction, so this run raises no corrupt-store finding, and says so in its docstring); a repair road (apply_memory_repairs) applying ONLY the derived safe repairs through the registry, returning every referred finding it did not apply with its plain refusal line; whole-book register and record roads; /memorydoctor on both surfaces (command handler and terminal, chat screen routed) - chosen over extending /doctor because that surface is the pre-existing shell-command fixer with its own grammar, while the `mythic doctor` CLI side is served by the new `memory` health check in doctor.py; journal-first finding, panel, verdict and repair news. NO config delta.

The readiness panel is derived from the whole book (every record carried whole, in a settled order - by derived mode, from-scratch first, then background, then fresh - then title, then record id - each row showing the entries usable now beside the stale entries still rebuilding), a cold-start verdict is derived for the whole book (cold while any project stands with no map, warming while any map rebuilds in the background, kind while every map stands fresh), and progress is derived per record against its plan. - Base verified in the worktree before work began: banked base a205373 (M-203 closure, 203/272) on yrsa/feature-roadmap-build, ls-remote verified at a205373 for that branch; team-02 stood reset clean at a205373 with no untracked scratch. - Roadmap words built to (roadmap_slices.yaml, M-204, Part 9): "The Juggernaut loop as runtime - inspect -> build -> test -> repair -> continue, per slice, without asking file/framework questions the code can answer; the loop's state machine is explicit and visible." Part IX - The Mythic Method Engine. The slice is built in the M-195 copy-and-share book shape the M-201, M-202 and M-203 books stand in.
- Charter finding (M-171, data/tui_redesign_charter.yaml): NO row of the charter names M-204 - the charter binds Part VIII alone (M-172..M-200) - and the M-005 method charter names no slice row either: its source note names the whole of Part IX (M-201..M-232) as the part that executes the charter and names YRSA_CODING_JUGGERNAUT itself among the six plugs (its F-04 tenet is the doctrine this runtime holds). The pure tests pin both facts live (test_charter_rows_do_not_name_m204). The slice is built to the roadmap words and that execution note together.
- Command name: /juggernaut stands free on the agent, the command handler, the terminal and the chat screen (checked before building - no prior road takes it). NO config delta: no config_defaults or M-009 catalogue setting is built or owed, in the M-199 manner.
- Built, pure layer (@075277d): mythic_agent/core/juggernaut_loop.py (2395 lines; 110 public names by live __all__ scan) + mythic_agent/data/juggernaut_loop.yaml (one example book "The Juggernaut loop at the M-203 slice boundary": 3 slice references, 5 runs, 2 views, 2 note records, 1 trace record, and its one pinned panel panel-m203-boundary under the every-run view; verdict strained at 3 sound of 5 under view-loop, open under view-sound; the data file's pinned panel was derived from the pure layer itself, so it agrees with the derived panel by construction). A loop run is held whole (the slice it runs, named by slice id, its title, the phases it walked in walk order, and the questions it asked, held by kind). The state machine is EXPLICIT and held as data (PHASES, TRANSITIONS): inspect steps only to build, build only to test, test to repair on a failure or continue on a pass, repair back to build or test for the rerun, continue steps nowhere. A run's standing is DERIVED at call time from its held phases and questions alone: a run that opens anywhere but inspect, steps where the machine does not allow, asks a file, framework, table or function question the code can answer (the human kinds - meaning, behaviour, values, direction - are the only questions the loop may ask), or has not yet reached continue stands unsound, named in its gaps. A run stands only for an ACTIVE slice: a run naming no held slice, or one that is not active, refuses BY NAME at book level. The run's trace - its walked phases as one line - is DERIVED at call time, and a held trace record stands current only while it agrees with the derived trace, stale beside it in the board. The juggernaut index, panel, verdict, board, trace, order and current run are DERIVED at call time, never stored where they could drift, and a stored one refuses BY NAME, as does a record claiming a loop was actually run live, a slice actually built, banked or pushed. The roadmap standing is proved, not asserted: roadmap_record loads this repo's own roadmap through the M-017 layer for real (272 slices, 11 parts, 203 done, M-204 standing queued at this slice's build time, next_slice M-204). The notes are held as data: a note record naming its run, its stance - note, concern, praise, question, a closed vocabulary - and what it feeds back toward, one record per run stance; holding a note posts none of it, the rule stands as data (JUGGERNAUT_RULE).
- Built, agent layer (@490f561): agents/llm.py (session JuggernautRegistry on _juggernaut_store, the 20 roads; juggernaut_status/panel/verdict and juggernaut_index derived at call time, never stored; the status also carries the derived board_record and the roadmap_record, and its plain_words is the derived index telling; register/record/view roads publish session news journal-first via the checkpoint target, deduped per shape - a run under its own run id and segment (record type juggernaut_run), a slice reference under its own slice id and state (juggernaut_slice), a view under its own view id, sequence and view filter, a panel under its whole derived shape, and a verdict under its word and tallies), agents/command_handler.py (/juggernaut routing + _handle_juggernaut), terminal.py (/juggernaut target + help segment), ui/screens/chat_screen.py (help line, usage entry, system-command routing). Honest boundary: holding, viewing, reading, reporting and telling run no loop, build no slice, execute nothing, bank nothing, push nothing, open no network and write nothing - runs are held as data, never performed live by this layer.

## M-207 Keeper Runtime - pure + agent layers BUILT (2026-11-10, team-02)

- Built, pure layer (@2b42f7e): mythic_agent/core/keeper_runtime.py (2404 lines; 110 public names by live __all__ scan) + mythic_agent/data/keeper_runtime.yaml (one example book "The Keeper runtime at the M-206 slice boundary": 3 slice references, 5 keepings, 2 views, 2 note records, 1 trace record, and its one pinned panel panel-m206-boundary under the every-keeping view; verdict held at 3 complete of 5 under view-keepings, reported under view-complete; the data file's pinned panel was derived from the pure layer itself, so it agrees with the derived panel by construction). The slice settles its shape from the tree first: Part V's keeper is M-104's keeper pattern (mythic_agent/core/keeper.py - a watcher judging generic targets, a dead background job or a crew member gone quiet, by the age of last activity), and this slice SPECIALISES it for campaigns in the M-201..M-206 copy-and-share book shape: one keeper per campaign, and the keeper's charge over one dealt slice held whole as a keeping (the slice it keeps, named by slice id, its title, the keeper steps it walked in walk order, and the evidence it carries, by kind). The keeper walk is EXPLICIT and held as data (CHECKS, TRANSITIONS): dealt steps only to watched, watched only to judged, judged to restarted on a stall or banked on a banking, restarted back to watched or judged for the rerun, banked steps nowhere. A keeping's standing is DERIVED at call time from its held steps and evidence alone: a keeping that opens anywhere but dealt, steps where the keeper sequence does not allow, rests on a bare claim - feeling, memory, assertion, summary - instead of held evidence (the held kinds - heartbeat_log, deal_ref, banked_ref, ledger_row - are the only evidence a complete standing may rest on), or has not yet reached banked stands open, named in its gaps: a stall is judged from held evidence alone, never from a feeling. A keeping stands only for an ACTIVE slice: a keeping naming no held slice, or one that is not active, refuses BY NAME at book level, and the next slice is dealt only when the current one banks - the current keeping is DERIVED at call time (the first held keeping not yet complete), so a slice already complete is never dealt again. The keeping's trace - its walked steps as one line - is DERIVED at call time, and a held trace record stands current only while it agrees with the derived trace, stale beside it in the board. The keeping index, panel, verdict, board, trace, order and current keeping are DERIVED at call time, never stored where they could drift, and a stored one refuses BY NAME, as does a record claiming a slice was actually restarted, dealt or reported live. The roadmap standing is proved, not asserted: roadmap_record loads this repo's own roadmap through the M-017 layer for real (272 slices, 11 parts, 206 done, M-207 standing queued at this slice's build time, next_slice M-207; the slice tests pin that build-time standing and the coordinator flips the pins at banking closure, as with M-206). The notes are held as data: a note record naming its keeping, its stance - note, concern, praise, question, a closed vocabulary - and what it feeds back toward, one record per keeping stance; holding a note posts none of it, the rule stands as data (KEEPING_RULE), and the keeper's reports - milestones, blockers and completion only - are likewise held as data, never sent.

A sentry's standing is DERIVED at call time from its held steps and evidence alone: a sentry that opens anywhere but named, steps where the sentry sequence does not allow, rests on a bare claim - feeling, memory, assertion, summary - instead of held evidence (the held kinds - campaign_ref, target_ref, drift_report, ledger_row - are the only evidence a complete standing may rest on), or has not yet reached reported stands open, named in its gaps: a watch is judged from held evidence alone, never from a feeling, and work drifting beyond the named target - wrong repo, wrong branch, extra features unasked - stands open by construction until it is caught against the campaign file, halted and reported. A sentry stands only for an ACTIVE slice: a sentry naming no held slice, or one that is not active, refuses BY NAME at book level, and the next slice is dealt with only when the current one reports - the current sentry is DERIVED at call time (the first held sentry not yet complete), so a slice already complete is never watched again. The sentry's trace - its walked steps as one line - is DERIVED at call time, and a held trace record stands current only while it agrees with the derived trace, stale beside it in the board. The sentry index, panel, verdict, board, trace, order and current sentry are DERIVED at call time, never stored where they could drift, and a stored one refuses BY NAME, as does a record claiming work was actually halted, drifted or reported live. The roadmap standing is proved, not asserted: roadmap_record loads this repo's own roadmap through the M-017 layer for real (272 slices, 11 parts, 209 done, M-210 standing queued at this slice's build time, next_slice M-210; the slice tests pin that build-time standing and the coordinator flips the pins at banking closure, as with M-209). The notes are held as data: a note record naming its sentry, its stance - note, concern, praise, question, a closed vocabulary - and what it feeds back toward, one record per sentry stance; holding a note posts none of it, the rule stands as data (SENTRY_RULE), and the watcher's reports are likewise held as data, never sent.
